achieve_silver_justification: WhitePact has already earned the OpenSSF Best Practices Silver badge (project 14112).
bus_factor_justification: WhitePact is currently founder-led with one primary maintainer. Continuity documentation exists, but a second maintainer with equivalent project knowledge and operational ability has not yet been established; this criterion will not be marked Met until that is real.
contributors_unassociated_justification: The project does not currently have at least two unassociated significant contributors meeting the OpenSSF Gold definition. This is an organizational maturity requirement and cannot be satisfied by documentation or automation alone.
copyright_per_file_justification: The repository has an MIT LICENSE with a project copyright notice, but source files do not yet consistently contain per-file copyright statements. This remains a technical Gold requirement.
license_per_file_justification: The repository is MIT licensed, but source files do not yet consistently carry per-file SPDX-License-Identifier statements. This remains a technical Gold requirement.
repo_distributed_justification: WhitePact uses Git, a distributed version-control system, and the authoritative public repository is hosted on GitHub.
small_tasks_justification: WhitePact publicly identifies bounded starter work for new and casual contributors with explicit scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria.
code_review_standards_justification: WhitePact documents what reviewers must check, security-sensitive review expectations, and technical acceptance criteria. The document explicitly distinguishes review standards from the separate two-person-review history requirement.
two_person_review_justification: WhitePact is currently maintained primarily by one person and cannot honestly demonstrate that at least 50% of proposed modifications before release were reviewed by a different person. This will only be marked Met after real independent review history satisfies the criterion.
build_reproducible_justification: WhitePact CI builds the wheel and source distribution twice from the same source revision with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH fixed to the commit timestamp, then compares SHA-256 digests. The first GitHub run of this gate completed successfully with byte-for-byte identical artifacts.
test_invocation_justification: The full automated Python test suite is invoked using the standard pytest command; CONTRIBUTING.md documents the exact commands and CI runs pytest directly.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs linting, typing, dependency auditing, tests with coverage, builds, Helm validation, accessibility checks, i18n checks, and a reproducible-build gate for pull requests and relevant pushes.
test_branch_coverage80_justification: WhitePact measures pure branch coverage with coverage.py/pytest-cov and has documented a verified 80.19% pure branch-coverage result with an 80% CI gate.
crypto_used_network_justification: Production deployment documentation requires secure HTTPS/TLS transport at the trusted ingress/reverse-proxy boundary; insecure public transport is not the documented production configuration.
crypto_tls12_justification: WhitePact's documented production deployment supports TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 and the reference deployment has been verified to negotiate TLS 1.3.
security_review_justification: WhitePact has a documented human security review/assurance process covering the security boundary, threat model, known gaps, and implemented mitigations. This is explicitly self-conducted and is not represented as an independent penetration test.
hardening_justification: The application implements defense-in-depth hardening including CSP/HSTS and related response headers, rate limiting, RBAC, tenant isolation, SSRF defenses, security scanning, and security regression tests.
dynamic_analysis_justification: WhitePact executes its production code through an automated pytest suite with pure branch coverage at or above the OpenSSF 80% dynamic-analysis threshold and enforces the branch threshold in CI.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The automated pytest suite uses extensive runtime assertions across governance, authorization, API, MCP, persistence, and security behavior during CI testing.
